intervals.quote: The MIMAC experiment is a directional detection project initiated in 2007 at the Laboratoire de Physique Subatomique et de Cosmologie (LPSC Grenoble-France) [22] in collaboration with IRFU-Saclay, CPPM- Marseille, IRSN and recently the Tsinghua University.

active_volume.note: Active volume as stated in the abstract for the detector with two independent chambers; the text gives 10.8 x 10.8 x 25 cm^3 per chamber.
active_volume.quote: the detector allows the reconstruction of the 3D tracks of nuclear recoils produced in the 6 liter active volume

summary.plain: MIMAC is a French dark matter experiment in the Modane underground laboratory. Its low-pressure gas chambers record the three-dimensional track of the nucleus a particle knocks, aiming to show which direction a dark matter particle came from. In 2026 it published its first directional limit.
summary.technical: MIcro-tpc MAtrix of Chambers: low-pressure (30 mbar) micro-TPCs, gas 50% i-C4H10 + 50% CHF3, pixelated Micromegas anode (424 um pitch) read every 20 ns by self-triggered electronics; bi-chamber module (two 10.8 x 10.8 x 25 cm^3 chambers) at the Laboratoire Souterrain de Modane since June 2012, unshielded. 2026: no excess towards Cygnus, sigma_SD-p < 6.65e-36 cm^2 (90% CL) from 495.1 and 354.2 day exposures. Next: MIMAC-35cm (twelve times the active volume, 100 eV threshold).

technology.quote: The MIMAC detector is a micro-Time Projection Chamber (µ-TPC) designed to measure both the kinetic energy and the 3D track of a recoiling nucleus.
technology.value: Low-pressure (30 mbar) gaseous micro-TPC with pixelated Micromegas anode and fast self-triggered electronics
